stories.title: Gartner Names Context Graphs Essential Infrastructure for Enterprise AI Agents, Predicts 50%+ Adoption by 2028
stories.body: In its September 15, 2026 report 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge,' Gartner identifies context graphs as the foundational layer that grounds AI agents in declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge required to reason about enterprise tasks, with policies enforced through runtime constraints. Gartner's separate August 2026 Emerging Tech Impact Radar names AI context platforms — citing Atlan, Databricks, Glean, Palantir, and Snowflake — as enabling technology for autonomous and multi-agent AI, with a 1-to-3-year window to mainstream adoption. Gartner projects that by 2028, over 50% of AI agent systems will rely on context graphs, while fewer than 10% have them today, and separately finds that only 6% of enterprises currently report meaningful ROI from AI.
stories.why: This is the single most powerful third-party proof point that the data foundation must come before agents work — directly validating the context-layer pitch and giving sellers a Gartner citation to use when a prospect says their existing knowledge base is 'good enough.' The 6% ROI statistic explains precisely why enterprise AI pilots stall and opens the door to a conversation about what is missing architecturally.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / CPG agentic AI
stories.title: McKinsey: For CPG Companies, Agentic AI's Real Payoff Is Growth — But Leaders Are Not Ready
stories.body: Published October 9, 2026, McKinsey's article draws on a survey of 41 senior commercial leaders at global CPG companies (most with over $10B in annual revenue) and finds that agentic AI can cut human effort in performance management by roughly half — tracking KPIs, detecting variances, and recommending actions — but questions whether leaders are ready to harness it. McKinsey's envisioned agentic workday has agents overnight synthesizing retailer performance, promotional results, inventory positions, digital-shelf metrics, competitive activity, and field execution data into a small set of prioritized opportunities and risks. A companion McKinsey report from October 28, 2026, surveying ~21,000 consumers, finds that companies are 'not yet equipped to meet the rising demand' for agentic commerce, with retailer AI assistants outperforming stand-alone platforms partly because they already have live inventory, payments, and delivery infrastructure in place.
stories.why: McKinsey naming the data infrastructure gap — live inventory APIs, clean catalog feeds — as the precondition for agentic ROI in CPG is a direct sales tool: retailers and CPG brands that lack a governed context layer will not capture the growth McKinsey describes. Sellers can use the 41-executive survey to justify urgency with procurement and the C-suite.

stories.title: Salesforce Completes $3.6B Acquisition of Fin (Formerly Intercom), Adding 30,000 AI Customers to Agentforce
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom) on September 10, 2026, bringing Fin's customer agent platform and more than 30,000 enterprise customers into the Salesforce Agentforce ecosystem. Fin's AI agent resolves chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack queries using a proprietary model called Apex, and has demonstrated resolution rates of around 76% of support volume end-to-end in some deployments. Salesforce's Agentforce business had already reached $1.2 billion in ARR in Q1 FY27 (up 20% year-over-year) before the deal closed, and Salesforce separately identified governance, knowledge quality, and enterprise data consistency as the primary blockers to AI service success.
stories.why: Fin is now a Salesforce product, meaning any enterprise prospect already on Salesforce CRM will face pressure to consolidate onto Agentforce + Fin — directly reshaping the competitive landscape for standalone agent vendors including Sierra, Decagon, and Cresta. The Salesforce-identified blockers (governance, knowledge quality, data consistency) are precisely the context-layer problems sellers should lead with to differentiate.

stories.title: Cresta Launches Conductor Self-Service Platform for Developers, Cuts Agent Deployment Timelines by ~50%
stories.body: On October 29, 2026, Cresta CEO Ping Wu announced the opening of Cresta's AI agent platform — called Conductor — to enterprise developers building customer-facing agents in-house or for clients, removing the requirement for Cresta's own deployment teams to be involved. Cresta says internal use of Conductor roughly halved initial agent deployment timelines; the platform provides end-to-end self-service for building, testing, deploying, and optimizing agents. Separately, Sierra introduced its Compliance Console on October 28, 2026, a set of configurable guardrails built into its Horizon platform that enforces locale-specific contact rules, frequency limits, and opt-out handling across channels, states, and countries.
stories.why: Both Cresta and Sierra made product moves in the same week — Cresta targeting build-in-house buyers with a self-service platform, and Sierra targeting regulated-enterprise buyers with compliance controls. Sellers competing beside or against these vendors now need to know Cresta's 'half the deployment time' claim and Sierra's compliance positioning, as both will surface in enterprise shortlists.

stories.title: Tredence Agentic AI Recovers $6.5M from $40M in Trade Deductions for Enterprise CPG Client Across 30+ Systems
stories.body: Tredence's agentic AI deduction-management solution, deployed for an unnamed enterprise CPG client, integrates across 30-plus systems — including SAP, EDI, retailer portals, and email — to evaluate each trade deduction, assign reason codes, and recommend next-best actions autonomously. The deployment recovered $6.5 million from approximately $40 million in addressable deduction spend, with the agent coordinating what had previously required manual review across fragmented back-office workflows. Tredence notes that Gartner projects 40% of enterprise applications will carry task-specific AI agents by end of 2026, up from under 5% the year prior, underscoring how quickly back-office agent deployments are moving from pilot to production.
stories.why: This is a rare named-outcome deployment in a real CPG back-office workflow — trade deduction recovery is a universal pain point for large CPG-retailer relationships, and the $6.5M recovery figure on $40M addressable spend gives sellers a concrete ROI anchor for supply-chain and finance buyers. The 30+ system integration requirement also illustrates exactly why a pre-built context layer matters before agents can act reliably.
